title: Welcome: How Our English Lessons Work
summary: This first lesson shows how an Ovi English lesson page works and helps the teacher find the student's English level.

cover.alt: A smiling young adult sits at a table at home, holding a phone that shows an English lesson page

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome to your first lesson with us! Today we will learn how our lesson pages work. We will also talk, so your teacher can learn about you.

blocks.title: Part 1: Tap a Word
paragraphs: This is a lesson page. It has a lot of words. Do you see a hard word? Tap it. A small window opens. In the window, you see the meaning in easy English. You also see the meaning in Japanese and in Spanish. Try it now. Tap the word window in this sentence. You can tap names, too. Then close the window and read more. Tap many words. It helps you learn.

images.alt: A finger taps a word on a phone screen, and a small window with the word's meaning opens above it

items.prompt: What opens when you tap a word?
items.answer: A small window with the meaning.

blocks.title: Part 2: Listen and Read
paragraphs: At the top of the page, there are three buttons: Study, Listen and Read. Study is the full lesson with check questions. In Read, you see the text in small pieces. In Listen, a voice reads the lesson to you. The words light up when you hear them. So you can listen and read at the same time. Each part also has a Play this part button. Tap it to hear only that part. You can change the help language, too. Use the English, 日本語 or Español button.

images.alt: A phone showing a lesson page with three buttons at the top, one word glowing yellow in the text, and earphones beside the phone

items.prompt: What happens to the words in Listen?
items.answer: They light up when you hear them.

blocks.title: Part 3: Questions and Practice
paragraphs: After each part, there is a short question. Answer it first, then read the answer below. Some lessons also have practice games. There are six kinds of exercise:

- Choose: pick the right answer.
- Match: join the two halves.
- Build: make a sentence from words.
- Fix: find the wrong word.
- Type: write the answer.
- Transform: change a sentence.
You always try first, and the answer comes after. You can stop and come back later. Your results are saved. Try the practice below now!

images.alt: A phone screen showing a practice game with four answer buttons, one of them green with a tick

items.prompt: I ___ a new student in this class.
items.explanation: Use am with I. Use is with he, she and it. Use are with you, we and they.

items.prompt: My teacher ___ English lessons every day.
items.explanation: In the present simple, add -s to the verb after he, she or it. My teacher is he or she.

items.instruction: Match each question with its short answer.
items.explanation: A short answer uses be if the question uses be, and do or does if the question uses do. The form changes to fit the person in the answer: Are you...? Yes, I am.

items.instruction: Make a sentence. Put yesterday at the end.
items.sourceJa: 昨日、私は友だちと映画を見ました。
items.answer: I watched a movie with my friend yesterday.
items.explanation: For the past simple, add -ed to most verbs: watch becomes watched.

items.sentence: This lesson is easiest than the last one.
items.explanation: To compare two things, use the -er form and than: easy becomes easier.

items.instruction: Make a yes/no question about her plan. Use be going to and add tomorrow at the end.
accepted: Is she going to study English tomorrow?
items.explanation: In a question with going to, put am, is or are first: Is she going to + the verb with no -s?

items.prompt: I have never ___ Mexican food. (食べたことがない)
items.explanation: Present perfect: have + the third form of the verb. Eat, ate, eaten.

items.instruction: Change it to the second conditional, for an idea that is not real now.
items.source: If I have time, I will learn French.
accepted: If I had time, I would learn French.
If I had time, I'd learn French.
If I had time I would learn French.
If I had time I'd learn French.
items.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, then would + the verb.

blocks.title: Part 4: Your Own Words
paragraphs: Do you want to remember a new word? Open the word's window. Then choose Save to My Words. The word goes into your own list. Save only the words you need. Now go to the bottom of the lesson. There you find My cards. Your saved words are here. Tap Learn to study your words. Tap Test to see what you remember. Do this for a few minutes after each lesson. Soon the new words will be easy for you.

images.alt: A hand holding a phone with a saved word on the screen, next to a small stack of word cards

items.prompt: Where can you find the words you saved?
items.answer: In My cards, at the bottom of the lesson.

blocks.title: Part 5: Lessons Made for You
paragraphs: At Ovi English, each lesson is written for one student. It starts from what you like and what you need. Do you love football, cooking or travel? Then your lessons can be about those topics. Every lesson also includes real facts about the world. So you improve your English and discover something new at the same time. The English is written at your level, not too easy and not too difficult. Class time is for conversation. Your teacher talks with you, asks you questions and listens carefully.

images.alt: A teacher and a student smiling and talking on a video call, with a lesson about football on the screen

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Lessons Made for You

items.answer: It is written from what one student likes and needs.

blocks.title: Part 6: Questions About You
paragraphs: Now let's talk, so your teacher can learn about you.

- What is your name? How do you spell it?
- Where are you from?
- Who is in your family?
- What do you usually do in your free time?
- What did you do last weekend?
- Where are you going to go on your next holiday?
- Think of two cities you know. Which one is bigger?
- Have you ever been to another country?
- If you could live in any country, where would you live?
- Some people say children should learn English very young. Do you agree? Why?

images.alt: A student talking to a teacher across a table, with speech bubbles full of question marks between them

items.prompt: Which question in the list uses did?
items.answer: What did you do last weekend?

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: Great work today, and now you can use our lesson pages on your own.
